glossary.diarrhoea: Passing loose or watery stools three or more times a day.
glossary.outbreak: More cases of an infection than expected in one place or group at the same time.
glossary.cruise ships: A classic closed setting for norovirus outbreaks.
glossary.care homes: Residential homes for older people, a classic closed setting for norovirus outbreaks.
glossary.subacute: Developing more slowly and lasting longer than an acute illness, but not chronic.
glossary.low-grade fever: A mildly raised temperature, usually 37.5 to 38.3°C.
glossary.clinical shock: Poor blood flow to organs, shown by cold peripheries, slow capillary refill and fast pulse.
glossary.clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing tests.
glossary.stool sample: A sample of faeces sent to the lab to look for the cause of infection.
glossary.IV fluids: Fluids given directly into a vein.
glossary.antimicrobial: A drug that kills or stops microorganisms, such as antibiotics or antivirals.
glossary.mature enterocytes: Fully developed absorbing cells at the tops of the villi.
glossary.absorptive surface area: The total area of gut lining available to take up fluid and nutrients.
glossary.lumen: The hollow inside of the gut.
glossary.mucosal invasion: Organisms getting into the gut lining itself, as with some bacteria, causing bloody diarrhoea.
glossary.immunisation schedule: The list of routine vaccines given at set ages in the UK.
glossary.lipid envelope: A fatty outer coat around some viruses that alcohol can dissolve; norovirus lacks one.
glossary.mainstay: The main part of the treatment.
